text:
maria: FYI — following up on the postmortem for the span-loss/aggregation issue. I sketched a remediation plan and need owners for each item.

incident-bot: Postmortem: https://redwood.internal/postmortems/rl-2026-span-loss — action items added to tracker.

sanjay: thanks. quick note: we still see the pattern every ~6 hours in prod where spans drop for ~2–5min and aggregations spike. I've attached a small log sample in the thread.

alex: can you paste the log lines here? easier to triage in-thread.

sanjay: sure —
```
2026-03-22T09:12:11Z service=ingest shard=7 WARN kv-cache: miss seq=124578
2026-03-22T09:12:12Z service=ingest shard=7 ERROR exporter: flush failed: 503 upstream write timeout
2026-03-22T09:12:15Z service=ingest shard=7 INFO aggregator: ingest-window closed, emitted 1.2x expected
```

emily: that 1.2x emitted is the double-counting we saw. looks like flush retries cause duplicate writes to the aggregator.

maria: OK — proposed action items: 1) Add idempotency keys at exporter layer (owner: ?), 2) Add a short-circuit backpressure when upstream returns 503 to avoid retries causing duplicates (owner: ?), 3) Backfill detection to find windows with >1.05x emission and alert (owner: ?), 4) Add end-to-end integration test that simulates exporter timeouts and asserts no double-counting (owner: ?), 5) Runbook + pager thresholds (owner: ?). Timeline: P1s 1–2 are 2 weeks, 3–4 are 1 week each, 5 in 3 days.

dave: I can take 1 (idempotency keys). estimate 3 days to land a safe change with canary.

sanjay: I'll do 2 (backpressure and retry policy). will try to have a design doc by EOD tomorrow.

emily: I'll own 3 (backfill detection) and 4 (integration test). I want to add a metric: `emit_window_multiplier` and a dashboard.

alex: I'll draft the runbook (5) and map thresholds to paging vs. slack alerts.

maria: great. small constraints: any code touching exporter must be non-blocking for Dedicated customers, so use async idempotency token flow, not global locks. dave — can you include that in your PR?

dave: yes. planning to use a short-lived dedupe cache keyed by (span_batch_id, exporter_instance) with TTL=2m. will include metrics for dedupe hits/misses.

emily: for backfill detection I'll run a job over the last 30 days to surface affected customers and generate a mitigation plan (rollback, re-emit, or correct aggregate). estimate 2 business days for results.

sanjay: design note: we should also examine KV cache eviction rates on shards that show the pattern. if cache thrashes during bursts we may see missing spans at the ingest side. I'll include cache metrics in the doc.

maria: good call. add `kv_cache_eviction_rate` and `exporter_retry_count` to the incident dashboard.

incident-bot: New task created: REM-4521 idempotency for exporter (assignee: dave).

maria: lets set checkpoints: design docs for 1/2 by 1769040000 (48h), PRs by 1769270000 (2 weeks), detection job results by 1769130000 (5 days). can everyone confirm?

dave: confirm.

sanjay: confirm, will post design link here.

emily: confirm. starting the backfill job now.

alex: confirm. I'll publish the runbook draft this afternoon.

maria: also — recurring pattern: this is the 3rd time in the last quarter where exporter upstream flaps led to aggregation drift. Ops suggestion: add automatic degraded-mode routing to a lighter aggregator variant for bursts. Not blocking the fixes but want a small spike mitigation that can be toggled. Thoughts?

emily: agree. we can add a routing rule in the smart router to temporarily switch to `aggregator-lite` if `exporter_retry_count > 100` in 1m. low-risk toggle.

sanjay: we should pair that with a canary policy so we don't lose fidelity for customers who need full signals. maybe route only non-critical customers during degraded mode.

maria: ok add as an optional mitigation (owner: alex for config + ops runbook). timeline: 3 days for a config toggle.

alex: noted — will add to repo and docs.

emily: one more thing — add an automated test in the CI that injects a synthetic 503 from upstream in the exporter canary and asserts no aggregate multiplier >1.01. I can add that as part of 4.

dave: adding idempotency will make that test pass.

maria: thanks everyone. I'll update the postmortem with owners/timestamps and send the first recap to the incident channel tomorrow AM. please update REM-4521/4522/4523/4524/4525 as you make progress.

alex: pinging product: @product — this will cause a short maintenance window for heavy ingest customers during the canary, FYI.

product: noted — we'll prepare comms and coordinate maintenance windows.

maria: closing loop: weekly check-in until all tasks are closed, then we'll run a retrospective to confirm the recurrence rate drops. next check-in: 1769080000 (in 1 day).

emily: ack.

sanjay: ack.

dave: ack.

maria: thanks, everyone.
